Leaked ‘GTA VI’ Soundtrack Is Real, With Cardi B, Travis Scott and Playboi Carti on Board

Last updated: November 16, 2026 8:14 am
By
DancehallMag Team
ByDancehallMag Team
DancehallMag is the leading independent publication covering Dancehall and Reggae music, the artists, and culture since 2019.
Follow:
1 day ago
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:50
Instaread

Travis Scott is apparently already in game mode. Days before Grand Theft Auto VI drops, he posted a photo holding a copy of the game in one hand and pizza in the other. Now the soundtrack he’s attached to has gone from internet rumor to confirmed fact.

That tracklist bouncing around social media? It’s real. Complex reports that a source close to the situation has verified the leaked lineup for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, a four-sided record with a guest list that reads like a festival poster.

The rap contingent is heavy. Playboi Carti, Cardi B, Gunna, JT and Travis Scott all appear, which tracks for a franchise that has always leaned on hip-hop to set the tone of its cities.

But this isn’t a rap-only affair. Dua Lipa, Tove Lo, Zara Larsson and Lana Del Rey are on there too. So is Morgan Wallen, who might be the biggest curveball on the list.

That spread makes sense when you think about how GTA has always worked. The series built its reputation on in-game radio stations, where you could flip from one genre to another mid-drive.

A soundtrack covering rap, pop and country fits the formula, even if it looks a little chaotic on paper.

For a lot of fans, the leak raised the obvious question of authenticity. Fake tracklists tend to spread fast whenever a release this big gets close, and plenty of people online weren’t sure what to believe until the confirmation came through.

Scott, for his part, seems more focused on the game itself. “What y’all on?” he wrote in the caption. “Tryna lock in. Beats, pizza, bring ya [own] controller. Who down?”

The game launches Nov. 19, and plenty of players will be loading up right at midnight. Preordering and predownloading is the move if you want to avoid headaches when the clock strikes 12.

Rockstar isn’t stopping at a digital launch either. Two days after release, the company is throwing Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival in Miami, with Travis Scott, Kodak Black and Cardi B among the performers.

The location is a pointed choice. GTA VI returns to Vice City, the franchise’s Miami-inspired setting, so staging a live event in the real-world version ties the music directly to the map players will be exploring.

Kodak Black’s name on the festival bill is interesting too, since he wasn’t among the soundtrack names reported so far.

It’s fair to assume the performers will lean on their soundtrack contributions, though nobody has said exactly what the sets will look like.

What’s still unclear is how the songs will actually show up in the game, and which artists landed original tracks versus licensed ones. With the album and the game arriving within days of each other, those answers won’t take long to surface.
